title: Municipalities
desc: 74th Amendment, Part IXA and urban local governance

basic.q: Which Constitutional Amendment Act gave constitutional status to urban local bodies (municipalities)?
basic.e: The 74th Constitutional Amendment Act, 1992 added Part IXA and the Twelfth Schedule dealing with municipalities.

basic.q: On which date did the 74th Constitutional Amendment Act, 1992 come into force?
basic.e: The 74th Amendment came into force on 1 June 1993, a few weeks after the 73rd Amendment (24 April 1993) relating to Panchayats.

basic.q: Municipalities are dealt with under which Part of the Constitution?
basic.e: The 74th Amendment inserted Part IXA, titled 'The Municipalities', into the Constitution.

basic.q: Part IXA of the Constitution spans which range of Articles?
basic.e: Part IXA covers Articles 243P to 243ZG, dealing with definitions, types of municipalities, their powers, finances and elections.

basic.q: Which Schedule was added to the Constitution by the 74th Amendment Act?
basic.e: The Twelfth Schedule, referred to in Article 243W, lists functional items that may be entrusted to municipalities.

basic.q: How many functional items are listed in the Twelfth Schedule?
basic.e: The Twelfth Schedule contains 18 items, including urban planning, water supply, sanitation and slum improvement.

basic.q: Which Article of the Constitution provides for the constitution of three types of municipalities?
basic.e: Article 243Q provides for constitution of Nagar Panchayats, Municipal Councils and Municipal Corporations.

basic.q: A 'Nagar Panchayat' is constituted for which kind of area?
o: An area in transition from a rural to an urban area
basic.e: Under Article 243Q, a Nagar Panchayat is set up for an area in transition from rural to urban.

basic.q: A 'Municipal Corporation' under Article 243Q is constituted for which kind of area?
basic.e: Article 243Q provides for a Municipal Corporation for a larger urban area, based on population and other factors.

basic.q: Which Article provides for the constitution of Wards Committees in municipalities?
basic.e: Article 243S provides for Wards Committees consisting of one or more wards, in municipalities with a specified population.

basic.q: Wards Committees under Article 243S are mandatory for municipalities with a population of what minimum size?
basic.e: Article 243S requires Wards Committees to be constituted in municipalities having a population of three lakh or more.

basic.q: Which Article provides for the constitution of a District Planning Committee?
basic.e: Article 243ZD mandates a District Planning Committee to consolidate plans prepared by Panchayats and Municipalities in the district.

basic.q: Which Article provides for a Metropolitan Planning Committee?
basic.e: Article 243ZE provides for a Metropolitan Planning Committee for every metropolitan area.

basic.q: A 'Metropolitan area' under the 74th Amendment refers to an area with what minimum population?
basic.e: Article 243P(c) defines a metropolitan area as one with a population of ten lakh or more, comprising one or more districts.

basic.q: Which Article deals with reservation of seats for Scheduled Castes, Scheduled Tribes and women in municipalities?
basic.e: Article 243T provides for reservation of seats for SCs, STs and women (not less than one-third) in municipalities.

intermediate.q:
Consider the following statements about the three types of municipalities under Article 243Q:
1. A Municipal Council is constituted for a smaller urban area.
2. A Nagar Panchayat is constituted for a larger urban area.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
intermediate.e: Only statement 1 is correct; a Nagar Panchayat is for a transitional (not larger urban) area, while a Municipal Corporation covers larger urban areas.

intermediate.q:
Consider the following statements regarding reservation under Article 243T:
1. Not less than one-third of the total seats are reserved for women.
2. Reservation for backward classes of citizens may be provided by the State Legislature.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
intermediate.e: Article 243T mandates not less than one-third reservation for women (including SC/ST women) and empowers state legislatures to provide reservation for backward classes, unlike the mandatory SC/ST reservation.

intermediate.q: Which of the following bodies is exempted from the application of Part IXA of the Constitution?
intermediate.e: Under the proviso to Article 243Q, industrial townships may be excluded, and Cantonment Boards constituted under the Cantonments Act are also outside the scope of Part IXA.

intermediate.q: Which Article empowers the State Legislature to entrust powers of tax collection and fund constitution to municipalities?
intermediate.e: Article 243X deals with power to impose taxes and constitution of funds by municipalities, distinct from 243W (functional devolution).

intermediate.q:
Consider the following statements about the State Finance Commission under Article 243Y:
1. It is constituted afresh separately for Panchayats and Municipalities.
2. Its recommendations cover both Panchayats and Municipalities.
Which of the statements given above is correct?
intermediate.e: The same State Finance Commission, constituted under Article 243-I, reviews the financial position of both Panchayats and Municipalities under Article 243Y.

intermediate.q: Article 243ZF, dealing with continuance of existing laws relating to municipalities, provides that such laws continue until amended or repealed, or until the expiration of what period from commencement of the Act, whichever is earlier?
intermediate.e: Article 243ZF allowed existing municipal laws inconsistent with Part IXA to continue for a maximum of one year from commencement (i.e., till 1 June 1994) unless amended earlier.

intermediate.q: Which Article makes Part IXA applicable to Union Territories?
intermediate.e: Article 243ZB extends Part IXA to Union Territories, subject to exceptions and modifications the President may specify.

intermediate.q: Which of the following functions is included in the Twelfth Schedule?
o: Regulation of slaughter houses and tanneries
intermediate.e: The Twelfth Schedule includes regulation of slaughter houses and tanneries among its 18 functional items entrusted to municipalities.

intermediate.q:
Consider the following statements on the Metropolitan Planning Committee (MPC):
1. It prepares a draft development plan for the metropolitan area as a whole.
2. Its composition is entirely nominated by the Governor.
Which of the statements given above is correct?
intermediate.e: Under Article 243ZE, the MPC prepares a draft development plan; not less than two-thirds of its members are elected by elected members of municipalities and panchayats in the metropolitan area, not nominated.

intermediate.q: Which Article vests the superintendence, direction and control of preparation of electoral rolls and conduct of elections to municipalities in the State Election Commission?
intermediate.e: Article 243ZA vests the superintendence, direction and control of elections to municipalities in the State Election Commission, on lines similar to Article 243K for Panchayats.

intermediate.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The 73rd and 74th Amendment Acts were both enacted in 1992.
2. Both Acts came into force on the same date.
Which of the statements given above is correct?
intermediate.e: Both amendments were passed in 1992, but the 73rd Amendment (Panchayats) came into force on 24 April 1993 while the 74th Amendment (Municipalities) came into force on 1 June 1993 — different dates.

intermediate.q: What is the normal duration of a municipality once constituted, under Article 243U?
intermediate.e: Article 243U provides that every municipality, unless dissolved earlier, continues for five years from its first meeting.

intermediate.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the District Planning Committee (DPC) under Article 243ZD:
1. It consolidates plans prepared by Panchayats and Municipalities in the district.
2. Not less than four-fifths of its members are elected by elected members of district-level Panchayats and Municipalities.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
intermediate.e: Both statements correctly describe the DPC under Article 243ZD, which prepares a consolidated draft development plan for the district.

intermediate.q: Which of the following is NOT among the 18 items listed in the Twelfth Schedule?
intermediate.e: National highway maintenance is a Union subject and does not figure among the 18 functional items in the Twelfth Schedule assigned to municipalities.

intermediate.q:
Consider the following statements about Article 243Q:
1. The Governor may specify an industrial township as exempt from constituting a municipality.
2. This exemption applies where adequate municipal services are provided by an industrial establishment.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
intermediate.e: The proviso to Article 243Q allows the Governor, by public notification, to exempt an industrial township providing adequate municipal infrastructure from having a municipality.

advanced.q: In Kishansingh Tomar v Municipal Corporation of the City of Ahmedabad (2006), the Supreme Court held that:
o: Elections to municipalities must be completed before expiry of the five-year term
Municipal Corporations can be dissolved without fresh elections indefinitely
State Election Commissioners can be removed by the State Government
Municipal reservation for women is unconstitutional
advanced.e: In Kishansingh Tomar v Municipal Corporation of the City of Ahmedabad (2006), the Supreme Court held that the constitutional mandate under Articles 243U and 243ZA requires timely elections before the term of a municipality expires.

advanced.q: The 'Nagarpalika Bill' that preceded the 74th Constitutional Amendment failed to secure the required majority in which House in 1989?
advanced.e: The 65th Constitutional Amendment Bill, 1989 (Nagarpalika Bill), passed the Lok Sabha but failed to get the required two-thirds majority in the Rajya Sabha; it was later revived as the 74th Amendment in 1992.

advanced.q: In K. Krishna Murthy v Union of India (2010), the Supreme Court, while upholding reservation in local bodies, held that:
o: Reservation for backward classes in local bodies requires prior empirical inquiry into backwardness
SC/ST reservation in municipalities is unconstitutional
Local body elections must be postponed until reservation is settled
advanced.e: In K. Krishna Murthy v Union of India (2010), a Constitution Bench upheld reservation under Articles 243D and 243T but held that reservation for backward classes requires a rigorous empirical inquiry and must not push total reservation beyond 50 percent.

advanced.q: The 'triple test' for providing political reservation to backward classes in local bodies (empirical inquiry, proportionality, and the 50% ceiling) was elaborated by the Supreme Court in which case?
o: Indra Sawhney v Union of India
Vikas Kishanrao Gawali v State of Maharashtra (2021)
Kesavananda Bharati v State of Kerala
S.R. Bommai v Union of India
advanced.e: In Vikas Kishanrao Gawali v State of Maharashtra (2021), the Supreme Court reiterated the triple-test conditions before local bodies (panchayats/municipalities) can reserve seats for backward classes.

advanced.q: Which Article bars courts from interfering in electoral matters relating to municipalities, similar to Article 243-O for Panchayats?
advanced.e: Article 243ZG bars interference by courts in matters relating to delimitation and allotment of seats, and provides that election disputes go only through an election petition.

advanced.q: Which Article of the Constitution excludes Part IXA's application from Scheduled Areas and tribal areas referred to in the Fifth and Sixth Schedules, unless Parliament extends it by law?
advanced.e: Article 243ZC excludes Scheduled Areas and tribal areas (Fifth and Sixth Schedule areas) from Part IXA, though Parliament may extend the Part with exceptions and modifications.

advanced.q: Article 243P(a) defines a 'Committee' under Part IXA to mean:
o: A Wards Committee constituted under Article 243S
advanced.e: Article 243P(a) defines 'Committee' to mean a Wards Committee constituted under Article 243S.

advanced.q: Which of the following correctly distinguishes the reservation scheme of Article 243T from Article 243D?
o: 243T applies to Panchayats and 243D to Municipalities
243T applies to Municipalities and 243D to Panchayats, but both follow a similar pattern of SC/ST and women's reservation
243D allows reservation only for women, not SC/ST
243T does not provide for women's reservation at all
advanced.e: Article 243D governs reservation in Panchayats while Article 243T governs reservation in Municipalities; both follow a parallel scheme reserving seats for SC/ST in proportion to population and not less than one-third for women.

advanced.q: Under Article 243T(6), which of the following statements about reservation for backward classes of citizens is accurate?
o: It is mandatory in every State
It is an enabling provision left to the discretion of the State Legislature
It applies only to Union Territories
It was struck down by the Supreme Court as unconstitutional
advanced.e: Article 243T(6) is an enabling provision — the State Legislature 'may' provide reservation for backward classes, unlike the mandatory SC/ST reservation under 243T(1) and (2).

advanced.q: Seats reserved for SCs, STs and women under Article 243T are required to be allotted, as far as practicable, by which method to different constituencies in a municipality?
advanced.e: Article 243T(5) provides that reserved seats shall be allotted by rotation to different constituencies in a municipality, similar to the scheme for Panchayats.

advanced.q: Which constitutional provision empowers the Union Finance Commission to recommend measures needed to supplement the resources of municipalities, based on State Finance Commission recommendations?
advanced.e: Article 280(3) requires the Union Finance Commission to recommend measures to augment the Consolidated Fund of a State to supplement resources of municipalities, based on State Finance Commission recommendations under Article 243Y.

advanced.q: The provisions of Part IXA relating to reservation of seats for Scheduled Tribes shall cease to have effect in which of the following?
o: States where the STs have no representation in the State Legislative Assembly
advanced.e: Article 243T(3)'s proviso clarifies that ST reservation shall not apply in a municipality of a State/UT where the Scheduled Tribes have no representation in the Legislative Assembly of that State or in the Legislature of that Union Territory.

advanced.q: Which of the following best explains why the 74th Amendment does not fully apply to hill areas of certain North-Eastern States having District Councils?
o: Because Article 243ZC exempts Sixth Schedule tribal areas from Part IXA
Because those areas have no urban population
Because those States are outside Indian territory for constitutional purposes
Because Article 243Q specifically excludes the North-East
advanced.e: Article 243ZC excludes Sixth Schedule tribal areas (which have their own District/Regional Councils) from the direct application of Part IXA.

advanced.q: Comparing the 73rd and 74th Amendments, which of the following is a key structural similarity?
o: Both created a State Election Commission and a State Finance Commission mechanism applicable to their respective local bodies
Both apply exclusively to metropolitan cities
Both were passed under Article 368 without state ratification
advanced.e: Both amendments rely on a common institutional design — a State Election Commission (Articles 243K/243ZA) and a common State Finance Commission (Articles 243-I/243Y) — reflecting their parallel drafting.

advanced.q: Which of the following statements about Article 243ZF (continuance of existing laws) is correct?
o: It automatically repealed all pre-1993 municipal laws immediately
It allowed existing municipal laws inconsistent with Part IXA to continue for up to one year or until amended, whichever is earlier
It applies only to laws made after 1993
It gave permanent immunity to pre-1993 municipal laws from amendment
advanced.e: Article 243ZF is a transitional/sunset provision allowing pre-existing municipal laws inconsistent with Part IXA to continue for a maximum of one year from commencement or until amended/repealed by the competent legislature.

title: Election Commission
desc: Article 324, appointment, powers and landmark rulings

basic.q: Which Article of the Constitution vests the superintendence, direction and control of elections in the Election Commission?
basic.e: Article 324 vests the superintendence, direction and control of the preparation of electoral rolls and conduct of elections to Parliament, State Legislatures, and the offices of President and Vice-President in the Election Commission.

basic.q: The Election Commission of India consists of the Chief Election Commissioner and:
o: Exactly two other Election Commissioners always
Such number of other Election Commissioners as the President may from time to time fix
Representatives of all recognised political parties
basic.e: Article 324(2) provides that the Commission consists of the CEC and such number of other Election Commissioners, if any, as the President may from time to time fix.

basic.q: On which date was the Election Commission of India established?
basic.e: The Election Commission of India was established on 25 January 1950, a day now observed as National Voters' Day.

basic.q: What is the tenure of the Chief Election Commissioner and other Election Commissioners?
o: 5 years or till age 62, whichever is earlier
6 years or till age 65, whichever is earlier
basic.e: The CEC and other ECs hold office for a term of six years, or until they attain the age of 65 years, whichever is earlier.

basic.q: The Chief Election Commissioner can be removed from office in the same manner as:
o: A Judge of the Supreme Court
A member of the Public Service Commission
basic.e: Article 324(5) provides that the CEC shall not be removed from office except in like manner and on like grounds as a Judge of the Supreme Court.

basic.q: Other Election Commissioners (besides the CEC) can be removed from office only on the recommendation of:
basic.e: Under the proviso to Article 324(5), any other Election Commissioner can be removed only on the recommendation of the Chief Election Commissioner.

basic.q: Which Act deals with the actual conduct of elections, administrative machinery and election offences?
basic.e: The Representation of the People Act, 1951 deals with the conduct of elections, disqualifications, election offences and disputes.

basic.q: The Representation of the People Act, 1950 primarily deals with:
o: Allocation of seats and preparation of electoral rolls
basic.e: The Representation of the People Act, 1950 provides for allocation of seats, delimitation of constituencies, and preparation of electoral rolls.

basic.q: Elections to Panchayats and Municipalities are conducted under the superintendence of:
basic.e: Local body elections are conducted by the State Election Commission under Articles 243K (Panchayats) and 243ZA (Municipalities), not the Election Commission of India.

basic.q: Electronic Voting Machines (EVMs) derive their legal backing from which provision?
basic.e: Section 61A of the Representation of the People Act, 1951 gives statutory backing for the use of EVMs in elections.

basic.q: Is the Model Code of Conduct legally enforceable in a court of law?
o: No, it is not legally enforceable and is based on consensus among political parties
Yes, but only during Lok Sabha elections
No, because it was struck down by the Supreme Court
basic.e: The Model Code of Conduct has no direct statutory backing; it is enforced through the moral authority of the Election Commission and consensus among political parties.

basic.q: The Chief Election Commissioner and Other Election Commissioners Act was enacted in which year?
basic.e: The Chief Election Commissioner and Other Election Commissioners Act, 2023 was enacted, replacing the 1991 Act on conditions of service.

basic.q: The 2023 Act on appointment of the CEC and ECs replaced which earlier legislation?
o: Election Commission (Conditions of Service of Election Commissioners and Transaction of Business) Act, 1991
basic.e: The 2023 Act replaced the Election Commission (Conditions of Service of Election Commissioners and Transaction of Business) Act, 1991.

basic.q: Delimitation of constituencies is carried out by which body?
o: The Delimitation Commission, a separate body under the Delimitation Act
basic.e: Delimitation is undertaken by a Delimitation Commission constituted under the Delimitation Act, a body distinct from the Election Commission of India.

basic.q: Which of the following elections does the Election Commission of India NOT conduct?
o: Election of the President of India
basic.e: Elections to Municipalities and Panchayats are conducted by State Election Commissions, not the Election Commission of India, which handles Parliament, State Legislatures, and President/Vice-President elections.

intermediate.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the history of the Election Commission's composition:
1. It was a single-member body from 1950 until October 1989.
2. It became a multi-member body for the first time on 16 October 1989.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
intermediate.e: The Commission was a single-member body from 1950 to 15 October 1989; it became multi-member on 16 October 1989 when two additional Election Commissioners were appointed ahead of the 1989 general elections.

intermediate.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The two additional Election Commissioner posts created in 1989 were abolished in 1990, making the Commission single-member again.
2. The Commission became permanently multi-member from 1993 onward.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
intermediate.e: Both statements are correct: the posts were abolished in January 1990, and the Commission became permanently multi-member again from 1 October 1993.

intermediate.q:
Consider the following statements about decision-making in the Election Commission:
1. The Chief Election Commissioner has a veto over decisions of other Election Commissioners.
2. Decisions of the Commission are taken by majority, as clarified by the Supreme Court.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
intermediate.e: The Supreme Court clarified that the CEC has no veto and is not superior in decision-making; decisions of the multi-member Commission are taken by majority.

intermediate.q: As per the Chief Election Commissioner and Other Election Commissioners Act, 2023, the Selection Committee for appointing the CEC and ECs comprises the Prime Minister, the Leader of Opposition in the Lok Sabha, and:
o: A Union Cabinet Minister nominated by the Prime Minister
The Speaker of the Lok Sabha
intermediate.e: Under the 2023 Act, the Selection Committee comprises the PM (Chairperson), the Leader of Opposition in the Lok Sabha, and a Union Cabinet Minister nominated by the Prime Minister.

intermediate.q:
Consider the following statements on salary and service conditions of Election Commissioners under the 2023 Act:
1. Their salary is equivalent to that of a Judge of the Supreme Court.
2. Their conditions of service can be varied to their disadvantage after appointment.
Which of the statements given above is correct?
intermediate.e: The salary of the CEC/ECs is equated with that of a Supreme Court Judge; Article 324(5) itself protects conditions of service from being varied to their disadvantage after appointment.

intermediate.q: The VVPAT (Voter Verifiable Paper Audit Trail) system was introduced into Indian elections through:
o: An amendment to the Conduct of Election Rules, 1961
A Supreme Court order creating a new statute
intermediate.e: VVPAT was introduced via an amendment to the Conduct of Election Rules, 1961, supplementing the EVM system already backed by Section 61A of the RPA, 1951.

intermediate.q: The introduction of 'NOTA' (None of the Above) in EVMs followed a Supreme Court directive in which case?
o: Kuldip Nayar v Union of India (2006)
Indira Nehru Gandhi v Raj Narain (1975)
intermediate.e: In People's Union for Civil Liberties (PUCL) v Union of India (2013), the Supreme Court directed the Election Commission to provide a NOTA option to voters.

intermediate.q: Which Article of the Constitution prohibits discrimination in electoral rolls on grounds of religion, race, caste or sex?
intermediate.e: Article 325 provides that no person shall be ineligible for inclusion in an electoral roll, or claim to be included in a special roll, on grounds of religion, race, caste or sex.

intermediate.q: Which Article provides for elections to the Lok Sabha and State Legislative Assemblies on the basis of adult suffrage?
intermediate.e: Article 326 provides for elections on the basis of adult suffrage, with the minimum voting age lowered from 21 to 18 years by the 61st Constitutional Amendment Act, 1988.

intermediate.q: Which Article bars interference by courts in electoral matters, confining challenges to election petitions only?
intermediate.e: Article 329 bars courts from interfering in matters of delimitation or the validity of laws relating to such delimitation, and provides that elections can be questioned only through an election petition.

intermediate.q: Registration of political parties, including allotment of symbols, is carried out by the Election Commission under which provision?
o: Article 324 read with the Conduct of Election Rules only
intermediate.e: Section 29A of the Representation of the People Act, 1951 provides for registration of political parties with the Election Commission.

intermediate.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Representation of the People Act, 1950 deals with delimitation and electoral rolls.
2. The Representation of the People Act, 1951 deals with conduct of elections and election disputes.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
intermediate.e: Both statements correctly describe the division of subject matter between the 1950 Act (rolls, delimitation, seat allocation) and the 1951 Act (conduct of elections, offences, disputes).

intermediate.q:
Consider the following statements about the Election Commission of India:
1. It is a permanent constitutional body.
2. It performs only judicial functions.
Which of the statements given above is correct?
intermediate.e: The ECI is a permanent constitutional body established under Article 324; it performs administrative, advisory and quasi-judicial functions, not merely judicial ones.

intermediate.q: Which of the following is a correct comparison of removal procedures under Article 324(5)?
o: Both the CEC and other ECs can only be removed like a Supreme Court Judge
The CEC can be removed only like a Supreme Court Judge, while other ECs are removed by the President on the CEC's recommendation
Other ECs can only be removed by Parliamentary impeachment
Neither the CEC nor other ECs can be removed under any circumstances
intermediate.e: Article 324(5) distinguishes the two: the CEC is removable only like a Supreme Court Judge (via Parliamentary address), while other ECs are removable by the President on the CEC's recommendation.

intermediate.q:
Consider the following statements on functions of the Election Commission:
1. It conducts elections to the office of President and Vice-President.
2. It conducts elections to Panchayats and Municipalities.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
intermediate.e: The ECI conducts elections to Parliament, State legislatures, and the offices of President and Vice-President under Article 324; local body elections are the State Election Commission's domain.

advanced.q: In Mohinder Singh Gill v Chief Election Commissioner (1978), the Supreme Court characterised Article 324 as:
o: A dead letter with no residual power
A reservoir of power enabling the Commission to act where the law is silent, to ensure free and fair elections
A provision limited strictly to counting of votes
advanced.e: In Mohinder Singh Gill v Chief Election Commissioner (1978), Justice Krishna Iyer described Article 324 as a 'reservoir of power' allowing the Commission to act to ensure free and fair elections where enacted law makes no adequate provision.

advanced.q: In T.N. Seshan v Union of India (1995), the Supreme Court upheld:
o: The single-member structure of the Commission as the only constitutionally valid form
The validity of the multi-member Commission and majority-based decision making among the CEC and ECs
The CEC's power to unilaterally overrule other Election Commissioners
Abolition of the office of Election Commissioners altogether
advanced.e: In T.N. Seshan v Union of India (1995), the Court upheld the 1993 restructuring into a multi-member Commission and held that the CEC does not have primacy over other ECs in decision-making, which is by majority.

advanced.q: In S.S. Dhanoa v Union of India (1991), the Supreme Court dealt with the constitutionality of:
o: The abolition of the two additional Election Commissioner posts in 1990
The removal of the CEC by impeachment
advanced.e: In S.S. Dhanoa v Union of India (1991), the Supreme Court considered the 1990 abolition of the two Election Commissioner posts created in 1989, and held that fixing the Commission's strength under Article 324(2) falls within executive discretion.

advanced.q: The Supreme Court's Constitution Bench ruling in Anoop Baranwal v Union of India (2023) held that, pending a law by Parliament, the CEC and ECs should be appointed by a committee comprising the Prime Minister, the Leader of Opposition, and:
o: The Speaker of the Lok Sabha
advanced.e: In Anoop Baranwal v Union of India (2023), a 5-judge Constitution Bench (opinion authored by Justice K.M. Joseph) held that, until Parliament legislates, appointments should be made by a committee of the PM, the Leader of Opposition, and the Chief Justice of India.

advanced.q: The CEC and Other ECs Act, 2023, enacted after Anoop Baranwal, differs from the Court's interim arrangement in that it substitutes which member of the selection committee?
o: It replaces the Prime Minister with the Vice-President
It replaces the Chief Justice of India with a Union Cabinet Minister nominated by the Prime Minister
It removes the Leader of Opposition entirely
It adds the Chief Election Commissioner as a member of his own selection committee
advanced.e: While Anoop Baranwal prescribed an interim committee of PM, LoP and CJI, the subsequent 2023 Act replaced the CJI with a Union Cabinet Minister nominated by the Prime Minister, a change that drew criticism for reducing judicial presence.

advanced.q: In Indira Nehru Gandhi v Raj Narain (1975), the Supreme Court held that which principle forms part of the basic structure of the Constitution?
o: Free and fair elections as part of democracy
advanced.e: In Indira Nehru Gandhi v Raj Narain (1975), the Court held that free and fair elections, integral to democracy, form part of the basic structure of the Constitution.

advanced.q: In Union of India v Association for Democratic Reforms (2002), the Supreme Court directed the Election Commission to ensure disclosure by candidates of:
o: Criminal antecedents, assets/liabilities, and educational qualifications
advanced.e: In ADR v Union of India (2002), the Supreme Court held that voters have a right to know under Article 19(1)(a), directing disclosure of candidates' criminal antecedents, assets and liabilities, and educational qualifications.

advanced.q: In Kuldip Nayar v Union of India (2006), the Supreme Court upheld amendments to the Representation of the People Act relating to Rajya Sabha elections concerning:
o: Removal of the domicile requirement and introduction of open ballot voting
Direct election of Rajya Sabha members by the people
Reservation of seats for women in the Rajya Sabha
advanced.e: In Kuldip Nayar v Union of India (2006), the Court upheld the removal of the 'domicile' requirement for Rajya Sabha candidates and the shift to an open ballot system, holding neither violated the Constitution.

advanced.q: Which of the following best describes the relationship between the Election Commission of India and the Delimitation Commission?
o: They are the same body under different names
The Delimitation Commission is a separate body under the Delimitation Act, though the CEC or a nominated EC and State Election Commissioners sit on it as ex-officio members
The Delimitation Commission is a subordinate wing of the ECI with no independent existence
The Delimitation Commission is headed permanently by the CEC
advanced.e: The Delimitation Commission is constituted separately under the Delimitation Act, typically chaired by a retired Supreme Court judge, with the CEC (or a nominated Election Commissioner) and State Election Commissioners as ex-officio members.

advanced.q: Electronic Voting Machines were first used experimentally in India in which year and location?
advanced.e: EVMs were first used on an experimental basis in 1982, in the Parur Assembly constituency of Kerala, before their nationwide rollout in general elections from 2004.

advanced.q: The Supreme Court order (2019, ahead of the general elections) that increased VVPAT slip verification from one EVM per constituency to five EVMs per assembly segment arose in a case filed by:
o: N. Chandrababu Naidu and other opposition leaders
advanced.e: Ahead of the 2019 general elections, the Supreme Court, acting on a petition by N. Chandrababu Naidu and other opposition leaders, directed VVPAT verification of five randomly selected EVMs per assembly segment instead of one.

advanced.q: Which of the following statements correctly reflects the protection given to Election Commissioners under the second proviso to Article 324(5)?
o: Conditions of service of the CEC and ECs may be varied to their disadvantage after appointment if Parliament so decides by ordinary law
Conditions of service of the CEC shall not be varied to his disadvantage after appointment
Only the salary of the CEC is protected, not other service conditions
There is no such protection in the Constitution
advanced.e: Article 324(5) itself provides that the conditions of service of the Chief Election Commissioner shall not be varied to his disadvantage after his appointment, insulating the office from executive pressure.

advanced.q: Which of the following is an accurate account of the timeline of the Commission becoming a permanent multi-member body?
o: Multi-member from 1950; single-member only briefly in 1993
Single-member (1950-1989); multi-member (Oct 1989-Jan 1990); single-member again (1990-1993); multi-member from October 1993 onward
Single-member throughout with no change till date
advanced.e: The correct sequence is: single-member (1950–1989), briefly multi-member (Oct 1989–Jan 1990), single-member again (1990–1993), and permanently multi-member from October 1993 onward.

advanced.q: Which of the following statements about the Election Commission's advisory jurisdiction under Article 103/192 is correct?
o: The Commission gives binding recommendations to the President/Governor on disqualification of sitting members, which they act upon
The Commission has no role whatsoever in disqualification matters
Only the Supreme Court can decide disqualification of sitting legislators
The Commission decides disqualification cases finally without reference to the President or Governor
advanced.e: Under Articles 103 and 192, questions on disqualification of a sitting MP/MLA are decided by the President/Governor in accordance with the opinion of the Election Commission, which functions in an advisory but effectively binding capacity.

advanced.q: Which statement best captures why the Election Commission of India is described as an 'independent' body, distinct from a mere department of the executive?
o: Its members are elected directly by citizens
It is created directly by the Constitution (Article 324), and the CEC enjoys security of tenure comparable to a Supreme Court Judge, insulating it from executive control
It has no accountability to any authority
It is controlled by the Ministry of Law and Justice on a day-to-day basis
advanced.e: The ECI's independence flows from its direct constitutional origin under Article 324 and safeguards such as the CEC's security of tenure and protected service conditions, which shield it from executive interference.

basic.q: Which Part of the Constitution deals with 'Services under the Union and the States', including Public Service Commissions?
basic.e: Part XIV (Articles 308-323) deals with Services under the Union and the States, with Articles 315-323 specifically covering Public Service Commissions.

basic.q: Which Article of the Constitution provides for a Public Service Commission for the Union and for each State?
basic.e: Article 315 provides for a Public Service Commission for the Union and a Public Service Commission for each State.

basic.q: Who appoints the Chairman and members of the Union Public Service Commission (UPSC)?
basic.e: Under Article 316, the Chairman and members of the UPSC are appointed by the President.

basic.q: Who appoints the Chairman and members of a State Public Service Commission (SPSC)?
basic.e: Under Article 316, the Chairman and members of a State PSC are appointed by the Governor of the State.

basic.q: What is the normal term of office of a member of the UPSC?
o: Five years or age 60, whichever is earlier
Six years or age 65, whichever is earlier
Six years or age 62, whichever is earlier
basic.e: Under Article 316, a member of the UPSC holds office for six years or until attaining the age of 65, whichever is earlier.

basic.q: Up to what age can a member of a State Public Service Commission hold office?
basic.e: Members of a State PSC hold office for six years or until they attain the age of 62 years, whichever is earlier, under Article 316.

basic.q: Under which Article of the Constitution can a member of a Public Service Commission be removed from office?
basic.e: Article 317 deals with the removal and suspension of a member of a Public Service Commission.

basic.q: Who alone has the authority to remove a member of a State Public Service Commission from office?
basic.e: Under Article 317, only the President can remove a member of a State PSC, even though the Governor appoints them.

basic.q: Which Article of the Constitution prohibits further employment of certain former members of Public Service Commissions?
basic.e: Article 319 lays down restrictions on further employment of the Chairman and members of PSCs after they cease to hold office.

basic.q: Which Article lays down the functions of Public Service Commissions, such as conducting examinations for recruitment?
basic.e: Article 320 lays down the functions of Public Service Commissions, including conducting examinations and advising on recruitment matters.

basic.q: Which Article gives Parliament or a State Legislature the power to extend the functions of a Public Service Commission?
basic.e: Article 321 empowers Parliament (for UPSC) or a State Legislature (for State PSC) to provide for the extension of the functions of a PSC.

basic.q: Which Article provides that the expenses of the UPSC or a State PSC are charged on the Consolidated Fund?
basic.e: Article 322 states that the expenses of the Union or a State Public Service Commission are charged on the Consolidated Fund of India or of the State, respectively.

basic.q: To whom does the UPSC submit its annual report under Article 323?
basic.e: Under Article 323, the UPSC presents its annual report to the President, who causes it to be laid before each House of Parliament along with a memorandum.

basic.q: To whom does a State Public Service Commission submit its annual report?
o: The Speaker of the Lok Sabha
basic.e: Under Article 323, a State PSC submits its annual report to the Governor, who causes it to be laid before the State Legislature.

basic.q: A Joint State Public Service Commission (JSPSC) serving two or more States can be created by:
o: A resolution of the State Legislatures alone
An executive order of the Governors concerned
An Act of Parliament on the request of the States concerned
basic.e: Under Article 315, Parliament may by law provide for a Joint State Public Service Commission (JSPSC) on the request of the State Legislatures concerned.

intermediate.q:
Consider the following statements about the term of office under Article 316:
1. A member of the UPSC may resign by writing to the President.
2. A member of a State PSC may resign by writing to the President.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
intermediate.e: Under Article 316, a member of the UPSC resigns by writing to the President, while a member of a State PSC resigns by writing to the Governor, not the President.

intermediate.q:
Consider the following statements regarding grounds for removal of a Public Service Commission member under Article 317:
1. Insolvency is a ground for removal.
2. Engaging in paid employment outside the duties of office during the term is a ground for removal.
3. Infirmity of mind or body is a ground for removal.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
intermediate.e: Article 317 lists insolvency, engaging in paid employment outside duties, and infirmity of mind or body as grounds for removal, in addition to misbehaviour.

intermediate.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. For removal on the ground of misbehaviour, the President must refer the matter to the Supreme Court.
2. If the Supreme Court holds that the member ought to be removed, the President is bound to remove that member.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
intermediate.e: Under Article 317(1), removal for misbehaviour requires a reference to the Supreme Court, and if the Court finds the member ought to be removed, the President is bound to act on that finding.

intermediate.q:
Consider the following statements about eligibility for further employment under Article 319:
1. The Chairman of the UPSC is ineligible for further employment under the Government of India or any State Government.
2. The Chairman of a State PSC is eligible for appointment as Chairman or member of the UPSC.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
intermediate.e: Both statements reflect Article 319: the UPSC Chairman cannot take further government employment, but a State PSC Chairman may be appointed Chairman or member of the UPSC.

intermediate.q:
Consider the following statements regarding a member (other than the Chairman) of a State Public Service Commission:
1. Such a member is eligible for appointment as Chairman of the UPSC.
2. Such a member is eligible for appointment as Chairman of that or any other State PSC.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
intermediate.e: Under Article 319(d), a member other than the Chairman of a State PSC is eligible for appointment as Chairman or member of the UPSC, or as Chairman of that or any other State PSC.

intermediate.q:
Consider the following statements about the reports of Public Service Commissions:
1. The UPSC's report is laid before Parliament along with a memorandum explaining cases where its advice was not accepted.
2. A State PSC's report is laid before the State Legislature by the Governor.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
intermediate.e: Both are correct under Article 323, which requires the report and an explanatory memorandum (on cases of non-acceptance of advice) to be placed before the legislature.

intermediate.q:
Consider the following statements about the composition of Public Service Commissions:
1. The Constitution fixes the exact number of members of the UPSC at eleven.
2. The strength and composition of the UPSC are left to the discretion of the President.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
intermediate.e: The Constitution does not fix the number of members of the UPSC; under Article 316, this is left to the discretion of the President.

intermediate.q:
Consider the following statements regarding suspension of a member of a Public Service Commission:
1. A member can be suspended by the President pending a reference to the Supreme Court under Article 317.
2. Suspension can be ordered even before the Supreme Court gives its report.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
intermediate.e: Under Article 317(2), the President may suspend a member against whom a reference has been made to the Supreme Court, even before the Court's report is received.

intermediate.q:
Consider the following statements regarding consultation with Public Service Commissions under Article 320:
1. The President or Governor may make regulations specifying matters in which it is not necessary to consult the Commission.
2. Consultation with the PSC on such exempted matters is not mandatory.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
intermediate.e: Article 320(3) proviso allows the President/Governor to make regulations exempting certain matters from the requirement of PSC consultation.

intermediate.q:
Consider the following statements about Article 316:
1. Members are appointed for a term of six years or until they attain the prescribed age, whichever is earlier.
2. The prescribed age is the same (65 years) for both UPSC and State PSC members.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
intermediate.e: Statement 1 is correct, but the prescribed age differs: 65 years for UPSC/Joint Commission members and 62 years for State PSC members.

intermediate.q:
Consider the following statements regarding Article 321:
1. It allows Parliament to confer additional functions on the UPSC in relation to services of the Union.
2. It allows a State Legislature to confer additional functions on the State PSC in relation to services of the State.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
intermediate.e: Article 321 allows Parliament and State Legislatures respectively to provide additional functions for the UPSC and State PSCs concerning their services.

intermediate.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the financing of Public Service Commissions:
1. Expenses of the UPSC are charged on the Consolidated Fund of India.
2. Expenses of a State PSC are charged on the Consolidated Fund of the State.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
intermediate.e: Under Article 322, expenses of the UPSC are charged on the Consolidated Fund of India, and those of a State PSC on the Consolidated Fund of the State concerned.

intermediate.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Parliament can, by law, provide that functions of a State PSC be exercisable by the UPSC.
2. This provision is found in the proviso to Article 315.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
intermediate.e: The proviso to Article 315 allows Parliament, on the request of a State, to provide that UPSC functions extend to that State's PSC functions as well.

intermediate.q:
Consider the following statements regarding removal on grounds other than misbehaviour under Article 317:
1. Removal for insolvency or infirmity does not require a Supreme Court reference.
2. The President can act on his own satisfaction for these grounds.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
intermediate.e: Only removal for misbehaviour mandatorily requires a Supreme Court reference under Article 317(1); for insolvency, infirmity, or outside paid employment, the President may act directly.

intermediate.q:
Consider the following statements about resignation and removal of PSC members:
1. A member of the UPSC can be removed by the President only in the manner provided in Article 317.
2. A member cannot be removed by any procedure other than that laid down in Article 317.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
intermediate.e: Article 317 is the exclusive constitutional procedure for removal of PSC members, ensuring independence of the institution from arbitrary executive action.

advanced.q: In State of U.P. v. Manbodhan Lal Srivastava (1957), the Supreme Court held that:
o: Consultation with the PSC under Article 320(3)(c) is mandatory and its breach voids the action
Non-consultation with the PSC under Article 320(3)(c) does not invalidate a disciplinary order nor give rise to a justiciable right
The PSC has binding authority over disciplinary decisions
Article 320 is not applicable to disciplinary proceedings at all
advanced.e: In State of U.P. v. Manbodhan Lal Srivastava (1957), the Supreme Court held that Article 320(3)(c) consultation is not obligatory, and failure to consult the PSC does not confer a justiciable right or invalidate the action.

advanced.q: In Ashok Kumar Yadav v. State of Haryana (1985), the Supreme Court laid down a principle concerning:
o: The age limit of PSC members
Members of a PSC recusing themselves from interviews of candidates related to them, to avoid bias
The salary structure of PSC members
advanced.e: In Ashok Kumar Yadav v. State of Haryana (1985), the Supreme Court held that a PSC member related to a candidate must not participate in that candidate's interview/selection, applying the principle against bias in selection.

advanced.q: How does the Supreme Court's role under Article 317(1) differ from an advisory opinion sought under Article 143?
o: There is no difference; both are purely advisory and never binding
Under Article 317(1), if the Court finds the member ought to be removed, the President is bound to remove; under Article 143, the opinion is advisory and not binding
Article 143 opinions are always binding, while Article 317(1) findings are advisory
Article 317(1) references are heard by a High Court, not the Supreme Court
advanced.e: Unusually, the Supreme Court's finding under Article 317(1) is binding on the President for removal of a PSC member, unlike an Article 143 advisory opinion which the government may choose not to follow.

advanced.q: Which of the following removal grounds under Article 317 do NOT require a reference to the Supreme Court before the President acts?
o: Insolvency, engagement in paid employment outside duties, and infirmity of mind or body
All grounds require an SC reference
Only infirmity of mind or body
advanced.e: A Supreme Court reference is mandatory only for removal on the ground of misbehaviour; for insolvency, outside paid employment, or infirmity, the President may act on his own satisfaction.

advanced.q: Which statement correctly distinguishes a Joint State Public Service Commission (JSPSC) from a State entering an agreement for shared administrative services?
o: A JSPSC requires no Parliamentary legislation, only a mutual state agreement
A JSPSC is created only by an Act of Parliament passed on the request of the State Legislatures concerned, unlike an informal administrative agreement
A JSPSC can be created only if all States of India agree
A JSPSC members are appointed by the Chief Ministers of participating States
advanced.e: A JSPSC is a formal constitutional body created only via an Act of Parliament upon request of the concerned State Legislatures under Article 315, with members appointed by the President.

advanced.q: Can the Chairman of a State Public Service Commission be subsequently appointed as a member (not Chairman) of the UPSC?
o: No, this is barred by Article 319
Yes, this is explicitly permitted under Article 319
Only with the Governor's prior approval
advanced.e: Under Article 319(b), the Chairman of a State PSC is eligible for appointment as Chairman or member of the UPSC, or as Chairman of another State PSC.

advanced.q: Which of the following best explains why the Constitution does not fix a specific number of members for the UPSC?
o: It was an oversight by the Constituent Assembly
Article 316 deliberately leaves the strength and composition to the discretion of the President, for administrative flexibility
The number is fixed by the Finance Commission
The number was fixed permanently at 9 by the Government of India Act, 1935
advanced.e: Article 316 deliberately leaves the number of members to the President's discretion, allowing flexibility to adjust the Commission's size as administrative needs change.

advanced.q: Are the recommendations/advice of a Public Service Commission on recruitment and disciplinary matters legally binding on the Government?
o: Yes, they are absolutely binding and cannot be departed from
No, they are advisory in nature, though non-acceptance must be explained via a memorandum placed before the legislature under Article 323
They are binding only for Group A services
They are binding only if approved by the Supreme Court
advanced.e: PSC advice under Article 320 is advisory; the government may depart from it, but must place reasons for non-acceptance in the memorandum accompanying the report under Article 323.

advanced.q: Which statement correctly reflects the historical origin of the UPSC?
o: The UPSC was first established by the Constitution of India in 1950

A Public Service Commission was first established in 1926 (following the Lee Commission's recommendation), later continued as the Federal Public Service Commission under the Government of India Act, 1935, and became the UPSC under the Constitution
The UPSC originated from the Indian Councils Act, 1909
The UPSC was created by the 42nd Constitutional Amendment
advanced.e: Following the Lee Commission's recommendation, a Public Service Commission was set up in 1926; it became the Federal Public Service Commission under the Government of India Act, 1935, and continued as the UPSC under Article 315 of the Constitution.

advanced.q: Which of the following is a valid distinction between the UPSC/State PSC and the Election Commission of India?
o: Both are governed by the same set of Articles (315-323)
The UPSC/State PSC are dealt with under Articles 315-323 (Part XIV), while the Election Commission is a distinct body under Article 324
The Election Commission is appointed by the Governor, like State PSCs
There is no distinction; they are the same constitutional body
advanced.e: The UPSC and State PSCs fall under Articles 315-323 in Part XIV, whereas the Election Commission of India is a separate constitutional body established under Article 324 in Part XV.

advanced.q: If the President suspends a Public Service Commission member pending an Article 317(1) reference, and the Supreme Court later finds no misbehaviour, what is the constitutional consequence?
o: The member remains removed regardless of the Supreme Court's finding
The suspension must be revoked and the member reinstated, as the President is bound by an adverse-to-removal finding as well
The matter is referred again to the High Court
advanced.e: Since the President's removal power under Article 317(1) is conditioned on the Supreme Court's finding, an SC finding against removal means the suspension should be revoked and the member reinstated.

advanced.q: Which of the following statements about Article 320(3) matters on which a Public Service Commission is normally consulted is correct?
o: Only examinations for civil service appointments
Methods of recruitment, principles for promotions and transfers, and disciplinary matters affecting a person serving under the Government, among others
Only disputes relating to pension calculations
Only matters relating to All India Services
advanced.e: Article 320(3) lists several matters for consultation, including recruitment methods, principles governing promotions/transfers, and disciplinary matters such as memorials or petitions.

advanced.q: Which of the following is an accurate statement on the number of members constituting a 'Public Service Commission' bench for disciplinary consultation?
o: A minimum of three members must always be consulted as a bench
The Constitution does not prescribe any specific quorum or bench strength; this is left to Commission regulations
Only the Chairman alone can give valid consultation
A two-thirds majority of all members is constitutionally mandated for every consultation
advanced.e: The Constitution does not prescribe a quorum or bench size for PSC consultations; procedural matters like this are governed by regulations framed under Article 318.

advanced.q: Which of the following correctly captures a subtle distinction under Article 319 between a UPSC Chairman and a UPSC member (other than Chairman)?
o: Both are treated identically and are equally ineligible for any future government employment
A UPSC Chairman is ineligible for further government employment, while a UPSC member (other than Chairman) is eligible for appointment as Chairman of the UPSC or of a State PSC
A UPSC member is ineligible for any employment, but a UPSC Chairman is not restricted
Only State PSC members are ever restricted; UPSC office holders are never restricted
advanced.e: Under Article 319, the UPSC Chairman faces the strictest bar (no further government employment at all), while an ordinary UPSC member may still become Chairman of the UPSC or of a State PSC.

advanced.q: Which of the following statements about judicial review of executive action taken contrary to PSC advice is correct?
o: Courts cannot examine such executive action at all, as PSC advice is purely internal
Courts can examine such executive action for compliance with Articles 14 and 16 (equality and equal opportunity in public employment), even though PSC advice itself is not binding
Only the President can review such action, not the courts
Such action is always struck down automatically for procedural impropriety
advanced.e: While PSC advice under Article 320 is not binding, executive action in service matters remains subject to judicial review for violation of the fundamental rights under Articles 14 and 16.

basic.q: Which Article of the Constitution provides for the constitution of a Finance Commission?
basic.e: Article 280 provides for the constitution of a Finance Commission by the President.

basic.q: At what interval must the President constitute a Finance Commission, at the minimum requirement?
o: Every five years, or earlier if necessary
basic.e: Under Article 280(1), the President constitutes a Finance Commission every five years or at such earlier time as he considers necessary.

basic.q: Besides the Chairman, how many other members does the Finance Commission consist of?
basic.e: The Finance Commission consists of a Chairman and four other members appointed by the President.

basic.q: Who appoints the Chairman and members of the Finance Commission?
basic.e: The Chairman and members of the Finance Commission are appointed by the President under Article 280.

basic.q: Which Act of Parliament prescribes the qualifications of the Chairman and members of the Finance Commission?
o: The Representation of the People Act, 1951
The Fiscal Responsibility and Budget Management Act, 2003
basic.e: The Finance Commission (Miscellaneous Provisions) Act, 1951, prescribes the qualifications for appointment as Chairman/members of the Finance Commission.

basic.q: Which Article requires the President to lay the recommendations of the Finance Commission before Parliament?
basic.e: Article 281 requires the President to lay the Finance Commission's recommendations, along with an explanatory memorandum, before each House of Parliament.

basic.q: Grants-in-aid to States out of the Consolidated Fund of India, recommended by the Finance Commission, are provided for under which Article?
basic.e: Article 275 provides for statutory grants-in-aid to States from the Consolidated Fund of India, on the recommendation of the Finance Commission.

basic.q: Who was the Chairman of the 14th Finance Commission?
basic.e: The 14th Finance Commission was chaired by Y.V. Reddy, a former RBI Governor.

basic.q: What share of the divisible pool of central taxes did the 14th Finance Commission recommend for the states?
basic.e: The 14th Finance Commission recommended increasing the states' share in the divisible pool of central taxes to 42%, a historic increase.

basic.q: Who chaired the 15th Finance Commission?
basic.e: The 15th Finance Commission was chaired by N.K. Singh, covering the award period 2021-26.

basic.q: Which census population data did the 15th Finance Commission use for its recommendations?
basic.e: The 15th Finance Commission used the 2011 census population data, departing from the earlier practice of using 1971 data.

basic.q: What share of the divisible pool of central taxes did the 15th Finance Commission recommend for the states?
basic.e: The 15th Finance Commission recommended 41% for states, a 1 percentage point reduction from the 14th Commission's 42%, due to the reorganisation of Jammu & Kashmir into Union Territories.

basic.q: Which constitutional body was established under Article 279A to deal with matters relating to the Goods and Services Tax?
basic.e: The GST Council, established under Article 279A by the 101st Constitutional Amendment Act, 2016, decides on GST rates and related matters.

basic.q: In which year was NITI Aayog established, replacing the Planning Commission?
basic.e: NITI Aayog was established on 1 January 2015 by a Cabinet resolution, replacing the Planning Commission.

basic.q: What is the nature of the recommendations made by the Finance Commission to the government?
o: Legally binding on the Union Government
Advisory in nature, not binding, though conventionally accepted
Binding only after ratification by the Supreme Court
basic.e: The Finance Commission's recommendations are advisory in nature and not legally binding, though they are conventionally accepted by the government.

intermediate.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the functions of the Finance Commission under Article 280(3):
1. It recommends the distribution of net proceeds of taxes between the Union and the States.
2. It recommends principles governing grants-in-aid to States out of the Consolidated Fund of India.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
intermediate.e: Both are core functions listed in Article 280(3)(a) and (b) — tax distribution and grants-in-aid principles under Article 275.

intermediate.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Finance Commission recommends measures to augment the Consolidated Fund of a State to supplement the resources of Panchayats.
2. This function is based, inter alia, on recommendations of the State Finance Commission.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
intermediate.e: Article 280(3)(bb)/(c) requires the Finance Commission to recommend measures to augment a State's Consolidated Fund for local bodies, considering State Finance Commission recommendations under Articles 243-I and 243-Y.

intermediate.q:
Consider the following statements comparing the Finance Commission and the GST Council:
1. The Finance Commission is constituted under Article 280, while the GST Council is established under Article 279A.
2. Both bodies deal exclusively with the same subject matter of GST rate fixation.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
intermediate.e: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the GST Council deals with GST rates, while the Finance Commission deals with broader tax devolution and grants, not GST rate fixation.

intermediate.q:
Consider the following statements about NITI Aayog and the Finance Commission:
1. NITI Aayog has taken over the constitutional function of tax devolution from the Finance Commission.
2. Tax devolution between the Union and the States remains a constitutional mandate of the Finance Commission alone.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
intermediate.e: NITI Aayog is a policy think tank with no role in tax devolution; that constitutional function under Article 280 remains solely with the Finance Commission.

intermediate.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the reduction of states' share from 42% (14th FC) to 41% (15th FC):
1. It was due to the reorganisation of Jammu & Kashmir into Union Territories.
2. The 1 percentage point was earmarked for the newly formed Union Territories.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
intermediate.e: Since J&K and Ladakh became Union Territories (not States), the 15th FC reduced the states' share by 1% to provide for these UTs from the divisible pool.

intermediate.q:
Consider the following statements about the qualifications of Finance Commission members prescribed by Parliament:
1. One member should be, or be qualified to be, a High Court judge.
2. Members may include persons with special knowledge of the finances and accounts of the government, or of economics.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
intermediate.e: The Finance Commission (Miscellaneous Provisions) Act, 1951 provides for members including a person qualified to be a High Court judge and persons with expertise in government finance or economics.

intermediate.q:
Consider the following statements regarding Article 275 and Article 282:
1. Article 275 grants are made on the recommendation of the Finance Commission.
2. Article 282 allows the Union or a State to make grants for any public purpose, even outside their legislative competence, independent of Finance Commission recommendation.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
intermediate.e: Article 275 grants are statutory and FC-recommended, whereas Article 282 discretionary grants do not require Finance Commission recommendation.

intermediate.q:
Consider the following statements about the term and reappointment of Finance Commission members:
1. The term of office of Finance Commission members is specified by the President in the order constituting the Commission.
2. Members are eligible for reappointment.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
intermediate.e: The President's order constituting the Commission specifies the term of office, and outgoing members are eligible for reappointment.

intermediate.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the 13th Finance Commission:
1. It was chaired by Vijay L. Kelkar.
2. It recommended a states' share of 32% in the divisible pool of central taxes.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
intermediate.e: The 13th Finance Commission, chaired by Vijay L. Kelkar, recommended a states' share of 32%, which the 14th Commission later raised to 42%.

intermediate.q:
Consider the following statements about the nature of the Finance Commission as a body:
1. It functions as a quasi-judicial body.
2. Its recommendations are enforceable by writ in the Supreme Court if not implemented.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
intermediate.e: The Finance Commission is a quasi-judicial body, but its recommendations are advisory, not enforceable by writ against the government.

intermediate.q:
Consider the following statements about Article 281 and Article 323:
1. Article 281 requires the President to lay Finance Commission recommendations, with an explanatory memorandum, before Parliament.
2. Article 323 requires a similar procedure for placing the UPSC's annual report before Parliament.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
intermediate.e: Both provisions follow a similar pattern of laying reports before the legislature with an explanatory memorandum: Article 281 for the Finance Commission and Article 323 for the UPSC.

intermediate.q:
Consider the following statements about the GST Council's composition:
1. It is chaired by the Union Finance Minister.
2. It includes the Union Minister of State for Finance and Finance Ministers of all States.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
intermediate.e: Under Article 279A, the GST Council is chaired by the Union Finance Minister and includes the Union Minister of State for Finance and State Finance Ministers.

intermediate.q:
Consider the following statements about acceptance of Finance Commission recommendations:
1. Parliament's approval is constitutionally required before the recommendations take effect.
2. In practice, recommendations are implemented through executive action and budgetary allocation once accepted by the government.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
intermediate.e: There is no constitutional requirement of Parliamentary approval; recommendations are implemented through executive action once accepted by the Union government.

intermediate.q:
Consider the following statements about horizontal and vertical devolution:
1. Vertical devolution refers to the distribution of the divisible pool between the Union and the States.
2. Horizontal devolution refers to the distribution of the States' share among individual States based on criteria like population, income distance, and area.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
intermediate.e: Vertical devolution is the Union-States split, and horizontal devolution is the inter-state distribution based on criteria such as population, income distance, area, and forest cover.

intermediate.q:
Consider the following statements about the first Finance Commission:
1. It was constituted in 1951.
2. It was chaired by K.C. Neogy.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
intermediate.e: The First Finance Commission was constituted in 1951 and chaired by K.C. Neogy.

advanced.q: Which of the following best distinguishes the Finance Commission from NITI Aayog?
o: The Finance Commission is an extra-constitutional advisory body, while NITI Aayog is a constitutional body

The Finance Commission is a constitutional body under Article 280 with a defined fiscal devolution mandate, while NITI Aayog is a non-constitutional executive body (Cabinet resolution) functioning as a policy think tank
Both are constitutional bodies with identical functions
NITI Aayog replaced the Finance Commission's function of tax devolution
advanced.e: The Finance Commission is a constitutional body (Article 280) with a specific fiscal devolution mandate, whereas NITI Aayog, created by an executive/Cabinet resolution in 2015, is a policy think tank with no constitutional status and no role in tax devolution.

advanced.q: Article 280(3)(d) empowers the Finance Commission to examine 'any other matter referred to it by the President in the interest of sound finance'. This provision illustrates that:
o: The Finance Commission's mandate is rigidly confined only to (a), (b), and (c)
The Finance Commission's mandate is flexible and can be expanded by presidential reference beyond the core listed functions
Only Parliament, not the President, can refer additional matters
This clause has never been used in practice
advanced.e: Article 280(3)(d) gives the Finance Commission a residuary, flexible mandate, allowing the President to refer additional matters connected with sound public finance.

advanced.q: The 15th Finance Commission's use of 2011 census data for population-based criteria generated controversy because:
o: It excluded southern states entirely from devolution

States that had performed better on population control (mostly southern states) feared losing relative share to states with higher population growth, prompting the Commission to introduce a 'demographic performance' criterion
It was the first time population was used as a criterion at all
It led to abolition of the income distance criterion
advanced.e: To address concerns of southern states (which achieved better demographic control) about the shift to 2011 data, the 15th FC introduced a 'demographic performance' criterion rewarding population control efforts.

advanced.q: Which of the following correctly distinguishes the Finance Commission (Article 280) from a commission constituted under Article 340 for backward classes?
o: Both are the same body with dual functions

Article 280 deals with fiscal devolution between Union and States, while Article 340 provides for a commission to investigate conditions of socially and educationally backward classes — an entirely different subject and body
Article 340 commissions also recommend tax-sharing formulas
Article 280 was inserted by the same amendment as Article 340
advanced.e: Article 280 governs fiscal federalism through the Finance Commission, while Article 340 is unrelated, providing for a commission on backward classes — a common distractor pairing in exams.

advanced.q: Who was appointed Chairman of the 16th Finance Commission, constituted in 2023?
advanced.e: The 16th Finance Commission was constituted in 2023 under the chairmanship of Arvind Panagariya, a NITI Aayog economist.

advanced.q: Which of the following are criteria used by recent Finance Commissions for horizontal devolution among States?
o: Population, income distance, area, forest cover, tax and fiscal effort, demographic performance
advanced.e: Recent Finance Commissions (14th and 15th) have used criteria such as population, income distance, area, forest cover, tax effort, and demographic performance for horizontal devolution.

advanced.q: Which of the following correctly explains why grants-in-aid under Article 275 are described as a statutory Union obligation, unlike tax devolution under Article 270?
o: Article 275 grants are charged on the Consolidated Fund of India each year as recommended, forming a specific statutory grant, while tax devolution under Article 270 is a constitutionally mandated share of a divisible pool rather than a discretionary grant
There is no meaningful difference between the two provisions
Article 275 grants are optional and rarely paid
Article 270 grants require annual Parliamentary re-approval while Article 275 does not
advanced.e: Article 275 provides specific statutory grants-in-aid charged on the Consolidated Fund of India, distinct from Article 270's constitutionally mandated sharing of the divisible pool of Union taxes.

advanced.q: The historical shift from sharing only specified individual taxes to a comprehensive 'divisible pool' of nearly all Union taxes was given effect by which constitutional amendment, based on which Finance Commission's recommendation?
o: 42nd Amendment Act, 1976, based on the 7th Finance Commission
80th Amendment Act, 2000, based on the 10th Finance Commission's 'Alternative Scheme of Devolution'
101st Amendment Act, 2016, based on the 14th Finance Commission
73rd Amendment Act, 1992, based on the 9th Finance Commission
advanced.e: The 80th Constitutional Amendment Act, 2000 implemented the 10th Finance Commission's 'Alternative Scheme of Devolution', pooling nearly all central taxes into a single divisible pool under Article 270.

advanced.q: A recurring grievance of States regarding the divisible pool relates to the Union's use of cess and surcharge. Which of the following is correct?
o: Cess and surcharge collected by the Union are fully included in the divisible pool under Article 270 and shared with States
Cess and surcharge are excluded from the divisible pool under Article 270, reducing the effective share received by States even when the headline devolution percentage is high
Cess and surcharge can only be levied by States, not the Union
The Finance Commission abolished all cesses in 2000
advanced.e: Under Article 270, cesses and surcharges levied by the Union are excluded from the divisible pool, meaning States do not get a share of this revenue despite a high recommended devolution percentage.

advanced.q: If the Union Government departs from a Finance Commission recommendation, what is the constitutional consequence?
o: There is no direct legal consequence, as recommendations are advisory; however, the government's decision and reasons are placed before Parliament along with the report under Article 281
The Supreme Court automatically strikes down the Union Budget
The President can dissolve the Lok Sabha over the disagreement
advanced.e: Since Finance Commission recommendations are advisory, there is no automatic legal consequence for departure, but the explanatory memorandum under Article 281 places the decision before Parliament for scrutiny.

advanced.q: Which of the following best captures the difference between the erstwhile Planning Commission's role and the Finance Commission's constitutional role in resource transfers?
o: Both performed identical constitutional functions of tax devolution

The Finance Commission's tax devolution/grants role is constitutionally mandated (Article 280), while the Planning Commission's plan-based discretionary transfers (like the Gadgil-Mukherjee formula) were extra-constitutional and administrative in nature
The Planning Commission's transfers were also governed by Article 280
The Finance Commission was abolished when the Planning Commission was created
advanced.e: The Finance Commission's role flows directly from Article 280, while the now-defunct Planning Commission's plan transfers (e.g., the Gadgil-Mukherjee formula) were extra-constitutional, administrative arrangements, now replaced by NITI Aayog's advisory role.

advanced.q: Which statement correctly reflects judicial treatment of Finance Commission recommendations if challenged in court?
o: Courts have held such recommendations create no legally enforceable right against the government, as they are advisory
Courts have held such recommendations are as binding as a constitutional amendment
The Supreme Court has original jurisdiction to modify Finance Commission awards
Such recommendations cannot be discussed in courts at all
advanced.e: Being advisory recommendations under Article 280, they do not create a legally enforceable right against the government, though they carry strong constitutional and conventional weight.

advanced.q: How many Finance Commissions had been constituted by the time the 16th Finance Commission was set up in 2023?
o: 15 preceding Commissions, making the new one the 16th
advanced.e: By 2023, fifteen Finance Commissions had already been constituted since 1951 (starting with K.C. Neogy's Commission), making the 2023 Commission the 16th.

advanced.q: Which of the following correctly explains the 'sound finance' residuary function of the Finance Commission in relation to fiscal federalism?
o: It confines the Commission strictly to a mechanical tax-sharing formula with no scope for broader fiscal advice
It allows the Finance Commission to be used flexibly by the President for emerging fiscal issues (e.g., disaster relief financing, fiscal consolidation roadmaps) beyond the core devolution functions
It transfers this function permanently to the GST Council
It applies only to Union Territories, not States
advanced.e: The residuary clause in Article 280(3)(d) lets the President use the Finance Commission flexibly for evolving fiscal concerns, such as disaster relief funding mechanisms or fiscal consolidation roadmaps, beyond the core enumerated functions.

advanced.q: Which of the following is the most accurate statement distinguishing Article 269A (GST on inter-state trade) from the Finance Commission's Article 280(3)(a) function?
o: Article 269A deals with apportionment of IGST between Union and States on inter-state supplies, administered per GST Council mechanisms, while Article 280(3)(a) is the Finance Commission's broader recommendation on sharing net proceeds of Union taxes generally
Article 269A and Article 280(3)(a) refer to the identical process
Article 269A was recommended by the 15th Finance Commission
Article 269A abolished the Finance Commission's role in tax devolution
